title: impSurface cannot be constructed without a GL context, which blocks all impCubeVolume testing
description:
impSurface::impSurface() calls glGenBuffers when mUseVBOs is true, which is its default on macOS. With no current GL context that segfaults. Verified: a program whose entire body is 'new impSurface()' exits 139.

The consequence is much wider than impSurface. impCubeVolume's own constructor does 'surface = new impSurface', so impCubeVolume cannot be constructed either -- and impCubeVolume is the marching-cubes pipeline, the single largest testable-looking surface in helios and hyperspace and the whole of gate criterion 1 (ss-53w).

So the triage ledger is wrong about it. impCubeVolume's functions are classified A, testable as-is, because the classifier reads each function's own source text and none of them names a GL call. The coupling is transitive and runs through a constructor, which regex rules cannot see. This is a false A, and false verdicts in that direction are the cheap kind -- work that looks available and is not -- but it has been steering the roadmap.

The fix that unlocks everything is small and local: the VBO ids are used in exactly three places, created in the constructor, deleted in the destructor, and bound in draw(). Nothing reads them between construction and the first draw, so generating them lazily at the top of draw() would make impSurface constructible without GL and change nothing for a real renderer.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately. It edits GL setup code that cannot be verified from a test binary -- there is no context to render against -- and ss-73x waived exactly this file to the Metal ports on the grounds that the port rewrites it. Making the change now would contradict that waiver in the same breath as recording it. It is a decision, and it is on the issue rather than in the code.

## Steps to Reproduce

Compile a main() containing only 'impSurface *s = new impSurface();' against Implicit/impSurface.cpp and -framework OpenGL, and run it outside any GL context. It exits 139.
design:
Three ways forward, and they differ in what they cost rather than in whether they work.

Make VBO creation lazy in draw(). Smallest change, unlocks impCubeVolume and roughly 300 regions of criterion 1 before the port. Cost: an unverifiable edit to rendering setup, against a standing waiver.

Fold impCubeVolume characterization into the Metal ports. Costs nothing now and matches the waiver, but it means the port proceeds with no safety net over the geometry pipeline -- which is the one thing the gate exists to prevent.

Give the test binary a headless GL context. Largest change, and it makes the test suite depend on the API the port is removing.

The first is the only one that gets a safety net in place before the code it protects is rewritten.
acceptance_criteria: impSurface is constructible in a test binary with no GL context, and impCubeVolume's triage verdicts reflect reality either way.
notes:
Ledger correction is partial and deliberately so. impCubeVolume::makeSurface carries a human B verdict in both submodules, as the public entry point and the thing a queue would dispatch against.

The private functions it drives -- polygonize, crawl_sort, crawl_nosort, calculateCornerMask, addVertexToSurface -- still read A in the ledgers. They are transitively blocked by the same constructor and are not reachable except through makeSurface, so the A is wrong for them too. Left alone because each correction costs a full instrumented rebuild and ss-or3 is blocked on this issue anyway, so nothing will dispatch against them in the meantime. Worth doing in one pass when this is resolved, whichever way it goes.

title: Define and hold the phase 1 to phase 2 gate
description:
"When enough code coverage has been accomplished, begin modernizing" needs a definition, or it becomes either a stall or a rubber stamp. This issue is that definition.

The wrong gate is a percentage. helios and hyperspace measure a 986-region denominator that is the shared C++ core only; hills measures 31 regions because Camera.m is the only non-GL, non-Cocoa unit it has. Driving those to 100% would leave Helios.cpp, rsText and HeliosView.mm -- the actual screen saver -- untested, because they are not in the denominator. A percentage of a denominator the port itself will redefine is not a gate.

The right gate is a safety net. Phase 2 changes the rendering path. What must not change is the geometry and colour that path consumes. So:

GATE, per submodule:

1. The modules the port feeds are characterized well enough that a change in their output fails a test. For helios and hyperspace that is impCubeVolume (makeSurface, polygonize, crawl_sort, crawl_nosort, calculateCornerMask, addVertexToSurface), impCubeTables, Rgbhsl and rsMath. impCubeTables, Rgbhsl and rsMath are done; impCubeVolume is not, and it is the bulk of what remains -- see ss-or3.

2. Bucket B is cleared or consciously waived, in writing. helios currently has 10 functions and 47 regions that need a refactor before they can be tested. Some of those refactors ARE the port, so waiving them into phase 2 is a legitimate answer -- silently leaving them is not.

3. Every new test survives a kill-check. Coverage that cannot fail is not a safety net, and this project has already caught itself writing three such tests.

Numeric proxy, useful but secondary: addressable ceiling of 80% for helios and hyperspace. Currently 25.9% each. It is a proxy because criterion 1 is what actually matters.

hills passes this gate today, trivially and for the wrong-looking reason: its only testable unit is covered and everything else is blocked on its port. hills is therefore free to start phase 2 now, and it is the submodule where porting buys the most coverage.
design:
Criterion 1 is named-modules rather than a number because the denominator is not stable across the phase boundary -- porting moves files into scope, so the percentage can fall while the codebase gets better. Anything gated on the percentage alone would misread that as a regression.

The gate is per-submodule on purpose. hills is ready and helios and hyperspace are not, and forcing them to move together would either hold hills back or start the C++ ports early.
acceptance_criteria: A written per-submodule verdict on all three criteria, recorded in this issue, before any port branch is opened for that submodule.
notes:
CRITERION 2 SATISFIED, 2026-08-21. Bucket B has a written verdict per blocker group, recorded in ss-73x: b:hidden cleared in phase 1 (declaration plus 9 cases), b:nondeterministic found to be a misfiled verdict and corrected in both ledgers, b:api-coupled waived to the two C++ ports with a stated condition -- the port must leave impSurface testable and move it into the coverage sources.

Bucket B in helios is now 3 functions and 37 regions, all of them the waived group, down from 10 and 47. Addressable ceiling 27.0% of 987 regions.

CRITERION 1 STILL OPEN. impCubeVolume is the remaining piece -- makeSurface, polygonize, crawl_sort, crawl_nosort, calculateCornerMask, addVertexToSurface. That is ss-or3 and it is the bulk of what stands between here and phase 2 for helios and hyperspace.

CRITERION 3 HOLDING. Every case written this session was kill-checked, and the discipline has already paid twice: three rsMath cases were passing for the wrong reason because their data had z = 0, and two apparent surviving mutants turned out to be bad mutations rather than test gaps.

hills verdict: PASSES the gate today. Criterion 1 is vacuous for it -- Camera.m is its only non-GL, non-Cocoa unit and it is covered. Criterion 2 has no bucket B entries. Criterion 3 holds; its 11 cases were kill-checked with 8 mutations. hills is clear to start ss-q1r whenever you want it started.

title: Phase 1 - a harness and coverage good enough to port against
description:
Goal one of two: build an effective test harness and raise coverage.

Done as of 2026-08-21: tools/coverage.sh (ratchet gate), tools/triage.sh (A/B/C classifier), /coverage-loop and its agents and skills, a PreToolUse branch guard, per-submodule CI, branch protection on the three forks, and a single-binary test harness with drivers in all three repos. Coverage went 0% -> 19.6% in helios and hyperspace and 0% -> 94.3% in hills.

What phase 1 still owes is NOT a bigger percentage. It is a safety net: enough characterized behaviour that phase 2 can change the rendering path and find out immediately if it changed anything else. See the gate issue for what that means concretely.

Read the numbers with their denominators. helios and hyperspace measure 986 regions -- the shared C++ core that compiles without a GL context. hills measures 31, because Camera.m is the only unit that is not GL or Cocoa coupled. Those denominators are not the screen savers; they are the part of the screen savers that is testable before the port.
design: This epic cannot reach the whole codebase on its own, and that is the finding that reshapes both goals. Coverage is capped by un-ported code: every coverage/<name>.json _scope block excludes the GL-coupled files and says the scope should grow as the port replaces them. Driving the current denominators to 100% would still leave Helios.cpp, rsText and HeliosView.mm untested, because they are not in the denominator.

title: Cut the two redundant coverage builds out of /coverage-loop
description:
Every iteration of /coverage-loop runs the instrumented build two more times than it needs to, and tools/coverage.sh wipes and rebuilds .coverage-build/<submodule>/ on every invocation, so each one is a full rebuild.

First: Stage 5 measures twice. verifier.md step 1 runs ./tools/coverage.sh --no-notify <submodule>, then coverage-loop.md line 139 re-dispatches coverage-runner, which runs the identical command against a tree nothing touched in between.

Second: Stage 1 re-measures an untouched tree. On iterations after the first, nothing changes between Stage 5 measuring and the next Stage 1 measuring again.

Fix both: have the verifier emit coverage-runner's report block (STATUS / pct / baseline / BASELINE_MOVED) from the run it already did and delete the Stage 5 re-dispatch; and have Stage 1 measure only on iteration 1, with later iterations reading the previous entry's coverage value out of loop-log.json.
design: Folding the measurement into the verifier does not violate the never-grade-your-own-work rule: the verifier is read-only and authored nothing in the wave. A reviewer who reproduced the gate green from a clean state is stronger evidence than a separate agent's number, not weaker. This is the largest wall-clock win available in the harness and is most of why a 3-iteration cap feels expensive.
acceptance_criteria: One gate run per iteration boundary instead of three. Stage 5 dispatches the verifier only. Stage 1 reads loop-log on iterations 2 and 3.
close_reason: Closed

title: Build the /coverage-loop pipeline: command, agents, skills, hooks
description: Replace ad-hoc skill invocation with an explicit orchestrated loop. A /coverage-loop slash command drives five scoped subagents (coverage-runner, triager, test-writer, refactorer, verifier) that follow four skills (coverage, triage, testing, refactor). Skills hold domain procedure, agents hold execution context and tool allowlists, the command holds the loop. Hooks in .claude/settings.json enforce the branch policy and syntax-check test edits.
design: Adapted to this repo rather than the generic design: tools/coverage.sh and tools/triage.sh are the runner and classifier, coverage/<name>.triage.json is the existing A/B/C contract so the triager selects from it rather than re-deriving it, the loop threshold is measured against the addressable ceiling not raw coverage, and test work happens on a branch inside the submodule (two PRs per the branch policy).
acceptance_criteria: /coverage-loop exists and runs; five agent definitions with scoped tools; testing and refactor skills written; hooks wired and executable; all four repos' branch policy respected by the loop.
close_reason:
Merged as fiazsami/screen-savers PR #7. The pipeline is built and has since been corrected against two independent audits: the command file, five agents, four skills and two hooks, with the redundant per-iteration rebuilds removed, the stop rule moved onto loop-log data, the verifier's restraint made checkable and routed through a different model, and the exit path fixed to re-attach submodules, stage the ledgers and carry evidence in the PR body.

It has also now been exercised end to end by hand rather than only reasoned about: the harness, drivers, gate, baselines, ledgers and two-PR submodule flow all ran for real this session across all three submodules.

title: Apply the branch policy to the three subrepos
description: With the policy established in the root repo, apply it to helios, hills, and hyperspace: enable GitHub branch protection on each master (require a PR, no direct pushes), and add a short AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md pointer in each so an agent working inside a submodule sees the rule without reading the superproject. Requires gh auth.
close_reason:
Both halves done. Branch protection is enabled on master in helios, hills and hyperspace: PR required (0 approvals), the 'tests' status check required, force pushes and deletions refused, enforce_admins off so a solo owner cannot lock themselves out. Verified by reading the protection back from all three. The AGENTS.md pointer landed in each repo via fiazsami/helios#3, hills#2 and hyperspace#2 -- it states the rules invisible from inside a submodule: never commit to master, pass -R to gh because these are forks and gh otherwise resolves to the parent, never commit from a detached HEAD, and a change here is two PRs with the pointer taking the merge commit rather than the branch tip.

Requiring a check meant first building one: there was no CI anywhere, so requiring a check would have made every PR unmergeable. .github/workflows/tests.yml now builds and runs each suite, green on real CI in all three repos before protection was turned on.

title: Regenerate the stale helios coverage baseline and triage data
description: coverage/helios.json and coverage/helios.triage.json were measured against the deleted fork's Metal-ported code. The re-forked helios is at v2.1.1, pre-Metal, so both files describe code that no longer exists and the ratchet gate would compare against a meaningless baseline. Re-run ./tools/coverage.sh helios and ./tools/triage.sh helios against the new tree and commit fresh data.
close_reason: Already done, verified rather than assumed. Re-ran ./tools/coverage.sh helios and ./tools/triage.sh helios against the current tree on 2026-08-21: both reproduce the committed data byte-for-byte, git status shows no change under coverage/. The ledger's 214 entries carry no Metal references, and the only 'metal' mentions in coverage/helios.json are in the _scope history block explaining that the port was lost with the deleted fork and pointing at ss-z2c. Commit 08214e4 re-scoped the config; the data was regenerated with it.

title: Rewrite branch policy and re-pin helios to the re-forked remote
description: The root repo's branch policy (CLAUDE.md:74) contradicts its own session-completion checklist, which ends at 'git push' rather than at an opened PR. AGENTS.md omits the branch rule entirely. Separately, the helios fork was deleted and re-forked, leaving the submodule pinned to a dangling SHA. Establish the new process in the root repo and re-pin helios, all via a feature branch and PR.
close_reason: Both halves verified done on 2026-08-21. CLAUDE.md carries the Branch & PR Policy section, declared authoritative over the generated session-completion block that ends at git push -- which was the contradiction this issue named. AGENTS.md now carries the branch rule (11 branch/PR references) rather than omitting it. And the helios pointer c585e43 is present on origin/master of the re-forked remote, so it is no longer a dangling SHA.

title: Record the two-phase project shape in CLAUDE.md
description:
CLAUDE.md describes the branch policy, beads and the session protocol, but says nothing about what the project is for. An agent reading it learns how to commit and nothing about why any of the coverage work exists.

Three things belong there, and the third is the genuinely non-obvious one:

1. The two goals -- build the harness and raise coverage, then modernize all three savers -- tracked as ss-1df and ss-23j with ss-53w as the gate between them.

2. That the gate is not a coverage percentage, and why. Porting moves files into the coverage scope, so the number can fall while the codebase gets better; anything reading the percentage alone misreads that as a regression.

3. That coverage is capped by un-ported code. Every coverage/<name>.json _scope block excludes the GL-coupled files and says the scope should grow as the port replaces them. helios and hyperspace measure a 986-region denominator that is the shared C++ core only. hills reads 100% on 31 regions because Camera.m is its only non-GL, non-Cocoa unit -- its coverage is blocked on its port, not the reverse.

Point 3 is what an agent will otherwise get wrong, and expensively: the obvious reading of 'raise coverage first' leads to grinding at a denominator that excludes most of the screen saver.
design: Offered during the realignment and deliberately not done, because it goes beyond revising issues and had not been asked for. Filed so it is tracked rather than dropped. Small -- a section, not a rewrite.

title: Clear or waive the bucket B refactor-first entries
description:
Criterion 2 of the phase gate (ss-53w). helios and hyperspace each have 10 functions and 47 regions that triage classifies as B: not testable until the code shape changes. Blockers, grouped: b:api-coupled (3 functions, 37 regions, worst is Implicit/impSurface.cpp draw()), b:hidden (5 functions, 8 regions, worst is rsMath/rsVec.cpp rsNormalize), b:nondeterministic (2 functions, 2 regions, worst is rsMath/rsMath.h rsRandi).

The point of this issue is that some of these refactors ARE the port and should be waived into phase 2 rather than done twice. impSurface::draw() is the obvious case -- it is api-coupled because it calls GL, and the Metal port is going to rewrite it anyway. Refactoring it now to make it testable, then rewriting it during the port, is work done twice with a characterization test that pins a shape about to disappear.

b:hidden and b:nondeterministic are different. Those are ordinary testability problems -- static linkage and an unseeded random -- that the port will not touch, and they are cheap. Those should be cleared in phase 1.

Deliverable is a written verdict per blocker group: cleared in phase 1, or waived to phase 2 with the port issue named. A silent leave-it is what the gate is meant to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three blocker groups has a recorded verdict; the ones marked 'clear now' are cleared and their functions are testable.
notes:
VERDICTS, recorded 2026-08-21. All three blocker groups ruled on, as the acceptance criterion requires.

b:hidden -- 5 functions, 8 regions -- CLEARED IN PHASE 1.
rsLength, rsNormalize, rsDot, rsCross, rsScaleVec in rsMath/rsVec.cpp. These had external linkage but no declaration anywhere, so no test could name them. That is the whole of what b:hidden meant here: not untestable, unreachable. Fixed by declaring them in rsVec.h, which changes no behaviour, no linkage and no generated code. Nine cases now cover them. Done in fiazsami/helios#5 and fiazsami/hyperspace#4.

b:nondeterministic -- 2 functions, 2 regions -- MISFILED, NOT A BLOCKER.
rsRandi and rsRandf are thin wrappers over rand(). Their contract is a range rather than a value -- 0 <= rsRandi(x) < x, 0 <= rsRandf(x) <= x -- and a range is assertable with no seed and cannot flake. Nothing needed to change to test them; the verdict was simply wrong. Corrected in both ledgers with tools/triage.sh --set, which preserves rule_would_say so the disagreement stays visible in the diff.

b:api-coupled -- 3 functions, 37 regions -- WAIVED TO PHASE 2, to ss-z2c and ss-a4a.
impSurface::draw() (31 regions), impSurface::impSurface() and ~impSurface() in Implicit/impSurface.cpp. These are api-coupled because they call OpenGL, and the Metal port rewrites exactly that. Refactoring them now to make them testable, then rewriting them during the port, is the same work done twice -- and worse, it would leave a characterization test pinning a shape that is about to disappear, which is a test that fails for the right reason at the wrong time.

The waiver is conditional, and this is the condition: the port must leave these functions testable and move them into coverage/<name>.json sources. That is not a favour to the gate, it is the mechanic the whole phase-2 epic depends on -- porting is what unlocks coverage.

RESULT. Bucket B in helios goes from 10 functions and 47 regions to 3 functions and 37 regions, all of them the waived group. Addressable ceiling 25.9% -> 27.0% of 987 regions. Criterion 2 of the gate (ss-53w) is satisfied: every group has a written verdict and nothing is silently left.
close_reason:
All three blocker groups have a written verdict, which was the acceptance criterion, and the two marked 'clear now' are cleared with their functions testable.

b:hidden cleared -- 5 free functions declared in rsVec.h, 9 cases covering them, merged as fiazsami/helios#5 and fiazsami/hyperspace#4.
b:nondeterministic cleared -- misfiled verdict, corrected in both ledgers; the range contracts were always assertable.
b:api-coupled waived to ss-z2c and ss-a4a, with the condition that the port leaves impSurface testable and moves it into the coverage sources.

Bucket B: 10 functions and 47 regions down to 3 and 37, all of them the waived group. Pointer bump in screen-savers PR #16.

title: Modernize the macOS platform layer in all three savers
description:
The Metal ports replace the rendering path. This is everything else the phrase 'macOS related updates' covers, and it applies identically to all three.

Measured 2026-08-21, same in helios, hills and hyperspace:

  MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET  10.9  -- from 2013, and it constrains every API choice below it
  NSOpenGLView                    -- deprecated since 10.14; 2 files per repo reference it
  ScreenSaverView                 -- 1 file per repo; the modern host API has moved on

Work this implies, to be confirmed per repo rather than assumed:

  raise the deployment target to something current, and decide what that costs in supported OS versions
  replace NSOpenGLView hosting with a Metal-backed view
  bring the ScreenSaverView subclass up to the current API, including the preferences sheet
  Xcode project settings: SDK, architectures (Apple silicon), build settings that predate them
  signing and notarization, which a .saver bundle now needs to install cleanly

Deliberately not folded into the three port issues. Those are about rendering and geometry, where the characterization tests apply; this is host integration, where they do not, and mixing the two makes a failed test ambiguous.
design: Sequence relative to the ports is a real decision and is not made here. Raising the deployment target first would simplify each port by making modern Metal APIs available; doing it after keeps the ports as pure renderer changes. Worth deciding once, for all three, before the first port branch opens.

title: Port hyperspace to Metal
description:
Second of the three ports. hyperspace shares the C++ core with helios but has the largest GL surface of the three: 13 files call GL or GLU, against helios's 4.

Follows helios rather than running alongside it. The two share Implicit, Rgbhsl and rsMath -- diverged per-entry, and the triage ledgers mark which entries are identical and which are not -- so whatever pattern the helios port establishes for separating geometry from rendering should be reused here rather than reinvented. A diverged twin has been touched by a port before and deserves more attention, not less.

Same two obligations as helios: the characterization tests must keep passing, and every GL file replaced with testable code moves into coverage/hyperspace.json's sources.
design: Depends on the helios port for the pattern, not for code. If the shared core gets genuinely unified rather than kept as two copies, that is a bigger change than this issue and should be split out -- it would also collapse ss-mws and half the duplicated test files.

title: Port hills to Metal, which is what unblocks its coverage
description:
Third port by size, first by coverage payoff, and the one that inverts the usual order.

hills reads 100% addressable coverage today. That is not an achievement, it is a 31-region denominator: coverage/hills.json scopes exactly one file, Source Code/Camera.m, because everything else is GL-coupled (HeightField, Scene, SkyDome, HillsOpenGLView, MainController) or Cocoa UI (PrefsController, URLTextField, HillsScreensaverView, main). The config's _scope block says so in as many words and ends with 'This list should grow as hills is ported.'

So for hills the dependency runs backwards from the project's default assumption: coverage is blocked on the port, not the port on coverage. There is no more meaningful coverage to add here first -- 6 files call GL or GLU, and none of the testable arithmetic is reachable around them.

hills therefore passes the phase gate today and can start now, in parallel with helios and hyperspace still finishing phase 1.

One live constraint from the tests already written: Camera's -render calls gluLookAt, so OpenGL is linked into the test binary and the tests deliberately stay off that method. The port should remove that link, and the tests should then cover -render.
design: Smallest saver and the clearest win, which also makes it a reasonable pilot if helios turns out to be too tangled to go first. The main argument for helios leading instead is that its core is better characterized.

title: Phase 2 - modernize all three screen savers
description:
Goal two of two: Metal port and macOS modernization for helios, hills and hyperspace.

Current state, measured 2026-08-21: all three target macOS 10.9, all three use NSOpenGLView (deprecated since 10.14) and ScreenSaverView. GL/GLU call sites: helios 4 files (Helios.cpp, HeliosView.mm, Implicit/impSurface.cpp, rsText/rsText.cpp), hills 6, hyperspace 13.

This epic does two things at once, and the second is easy to lose sight of. It modernizes the savers, and it *unlocks coverage* -- every GL-coupled file it replaces with testable code is a file that can move into a coverage config's sources. hills is the clearest case: it sits at 100% of a 31-region denominator only because everything else is GL or Cocoa. Its coverage is blocked on its port, not the other way round.
design:
Gated on phase 1, but not on a coverage percentage -- on having the behaviour the port will touch characterized. See the gate issue.

The ordering within this epic is deliberate: helios first because its shared core is the best covered and its GL surface is the smallest (4 files), hyperspace second because it shares that core but has 13 GL files, hills last on the port and first on the coverage payoff.

title: guard-default-branch.py cannot see commits made by cherry-pick, merge, revert or rebase
description:
The PreToolUse guard parses the Bash command and only acts on git subcommands 'commit' and 'push'. Every other way git creates a commit is invisible to it: cherry-pick, merge, revert, rebase --continue, am, and stash pop with conflicts resolved into a commit.

Hit for real on 2026-08-21. A 'git cherry-pick <sha>' run while HEAD was main created a commit on the default branch and the guard allowed it, because the word 'commit' never appeared in the command. It was caught by reading git status afterwards, not by the hook, and nothing had been pushed.

The fix is to treat the subcommand list as the thing that is wrong. Refuse any of cherry-pick, merge, revert, rebase, am while HEAD is the repo default branch -- with the same fail-open behaviour on its own errors, and the same detached-HEAD handling already added for commit.

Worth noting what this does not change: the guard remains a backstop for the honest mistake, not a security boundary. A commit created by a script the hook cannot introspect is still invisible, which is the same limitation recorded in the docstring for gh pr merge.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On main in the superproject, with any commit on a feature branch.
2. Run git cherry-pick <that sha>.
3. The commit lands on main and the guard says nothing. Expected: refused, exactly as git commit on main is refused.
design: Found by making the mistake, which is the failure mode the guard exists to catch. Also an argument for the fingerprint pattern used around the verifier: checking the resulting state catches what command-shape matching misses.
acceptance_criteria: git cherry-pick, merge, revert and rebase are all refused while HEAD is a default branch; a repo with no origin/HEAD and no main/master still passes quietly.
close_reason:
Merged as fiazsami/screen-savers PR #13. The guard now refuses commit, cherry-pick, merge, revert, rebase and am while HEAD is a default branch or detached, with merge --ff-only and pull exempt since neither can create a commit. Verified across 15 cases against a scratch repo.

Still not a security boundary, and the docstring says so: a commit created by a script the hook cannot introspect remains invisible.

title: Characterize impCubeVolume - the core the port must not change
description:
The gate is armed in all three submodules but helios and hyperspace sit at 5.4%, with an addressable ceiling of 5.1% of 986 regions each. The shared C++ core is where nearly all of that is.

From the triage ledgers, worst-first: impCubeVolume::makeSurface overloads (119 and 116 uncovered regions in hyperspace), impCubeTables::makeCrawlDirections (73), impCubeTables::makeTriStripPatterns (42), impCubeVolume::calculateCornerMask (33), crawl_nosort (30), crawl_sort (28), polygonize (25, verdict A recorded in ss-823).

rsMath is the other obvious target and is mostly pure functions.

Note helios and hyperspace carry copies of this core that the ledgers mark shared_copy identical or diverged per entry. Cover one copy, check the twin's marker, and port rather than rewriting -- a diverged twin has been touched by a port and deserves more attention, not less.
design: This is what /coverage-loop was built to drive. Now that the harness, the baselines and the ledgers all exist, it can actually be run against these two rather than done by hand.
acceptance_criteria: Addressable ceiling for helios and hyperspace materially above 5.1%, with every new case kill-checked.
notes:
BLOCKED 2026-08-21 by ss-aio, discovered while attempting exactly this work.

impCubeVolume cannot be constructed in a test binary. Its constructor does 'surface = new impSurface', and impSurface's constructor calls glGenBuffers, which segfaults with no GL context. Verified directly: a program whose whole body is 'new impSurface()' exits 139.

So the remaining scope of this issue -- makeSurface, polygonize, crawl_sort, crawl_nosort, calculateCornerMask, addVertexToSurface -- is not reachable at all today, not merely hard. The triage ledger classifies these A because the classifier reads each function's own text and none of them names a GL call; the coupling is transitive through a constructor, which regex rules cannot see.

Two smaller findings from the attempt, both still true and worth keeping:

impSurface has no getters. Every geometry field is private and draw() is the only reader, so even with a constructible impSurface a test could call makeSurface() and assert nothing about the result. Read-only accessors are needed as well -- and note they must expose vertex_offset/6 rather than vertices.size()/6, because the vectors are over-allocated in blocks of 1000.

The test design was sound and should be reused once unblocked: an analytic sphere as the field, then assert every emitted vertex lies on it within a fraction of the cube width. That validates the corner mask, the crawl and the strip patterns against geometry rather than against a golden run.

title: Decide how the superproject gets a server-enforced review gate
description:
This is a decision, not an implementation, and it blocks any automated ship harness.

Verified current state of the four repos. helios, hills and hyperspace are public forks with no branch protection -- the protection endpoint returns 404 branch not protected and rulesets is empty, both fixable with a single gh api PUT. fiazsami/screen-savers is a private repo on a free plan, where both the branch-protection and the rulesets endpoints return 403 upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public. There is no configuration that puts protection on the superproject default branch as things stand.

So the choice is: make screen-savers public, pay for Pro, or accept that nothing server-side gates the superproject merge and that a script's own polling is the entire gate. The third is defensible, but only if the polling then fails closed on a missing check rather than treating absent as passed -- because it becomes load-bearing rather than belt-and-braces.

There is a second half to the decision, which matters more than strict-versus-permissive: what artifact constitutes review. A check-run conclusion, a reviewDecision, or a human. Only the first can work unattended, and only if the review is exposed as a check run under an exact known name. A required approving review instead parks mergeStateStatus at BLOCKED -- a bot review generally does not satisfy it and an author cannot approve their own PR -- so every PR would burn its full timeout and report a failure. Answer that first; strict versus permissive follows from it.

Worth noting the asymmetry: the three repos that can be protected are the ones whose PRs carry the actual code and merge first. The one that cannot carries only pointers and baselines. That is the more forgiving way round, and it is luck rather than design.
design: Sources: harness-build-instructions-review.md sections 2.1 through 2.4 and ship-harness-audit.md sections 1.2 and 2.3. Also relevant: a submodule PR cannot be verified in its own repo, since coverage.sh, the configs and the baselines all live in the superproject -- so whatever gate is chosen, the submodule review is the last one that can still stop the work, and submodule merges are irreversible in practice.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision naming the review artifact and the superproject's gate, with the submodule protection applied if that is the outcome.
notes:
REALIGNED 2026-08-21: this is phase 1 harness infrastructure, not a blocker on phase 2.

The three forks now have branch protection requiring the 'tests' check, so the repos that carry the actual port work are gated. Only the superproject is unprotected, and its PRs carry pointers and baselines rather than code. That is the forgiving way round, so this does not hold up the ports -- it is left open because the decision is still real, not because anything waits on it.

title: Correct the /coverage-loop exit path: re-attach, stage ledgers, carry evidence
description:
Four corrections to the exit path in .claude/commands/coverage-loop.md.

Re-attach the submodules. Recording a pointer leaves each submodule detached at the merge sha, which is correct for the bump and wrong as a resting state -- Stage 0 step 2 refuses to start when any submodule is detached, so the success path is the next run's blocked preflight. Re-attach with git switch <default> and git pull --ff-only, and do it after the superproject PR merges, not after the bump: until then the default branch is not yet where the pointer says it is.

Stage the triage ledgers with the baselines. Step 3 mentions only baseline files. The ledger is the evidence for what the run decided not to test, and it belongs in the same commit as the ratchet advance -- otherwise it stays modified and the superproject preflight fails.

Carry the evidence in the PR body, not as a path. Step 2 relies on reviewers seeing the loop log, but .claude/artifacts/loop-log.json is gitignored and does not exist in the submodule repos at all -- a reviewer opening a helios PR gets a pointer to an uncommitted file in a different repository. Paste the iteration's loop-log entry and the verifier findings into the body. Say plainly why, too: a submodule PR reviewer cannot run the gate, because coverage.sh, the configs and the baselines all live in the superproject. The verifier report is the only evidence that PR carries.

Handle zero submodule merges. The gate rewrites the superproject baselines and ledgers on every run, so zero submodule merges does not mean nothing to ship -- it means ship the superproject alone, or discard the measurement and say so. As written the run ends with a dirty superproject tree and an uncommitted ratchet advance.
design: Sources: harness-build-instructions-review.md sections 4.3, 1.2, 5.2 and 5.3; ship-harness-audit.md sections 4.4, 4.6, 5.1 and 5.4. The re-attach item pairs with the detached-HEAD guard bug -- with that fixed the failure at least becomes loud instead of silent.
acceptance_criteria: After a full run, no submodule is left detached. The superproject tree is clean. A submodule PR body contains the verifier findings and the iteration's numbers rather than a path to them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix /coverage-loop Stage 0 preflight: generated files and pre-existing branches
description:
Two preflight defects that fire on the loop's own output.

Dirty-tree check (coverage-loop.md lines 29-32). Stage 2 rewrites coverage/*.triage.json every iteration and those files are tracked, so a resumed run's preflight trips on work the loop itself did. Separately, default git status --porcelain reports a submodule as modified for untracked content inside it, so one stray .DS_Store in helios fails the preflight as dirty tree with no indication which repo caused it. Fix: check with --ignore-submodules=untracked, and treat coverage/*.triage.json and coverage/*.baseline.json as expected-generated by name -- anything else dirty still stops the run.

Pre-existing branch (step 3). Nothing in the harness deletes test/coverage-loop, and the exit path that says to delete it does not. A second run's git switch -c collides with the stale local branch. Fix: if the branch already exists, either resume onto it by reading loop-log, or stop and say so -- and make the exit path actually perform the deletes, local and remote.

## Steps to Reproduce

Generated files: run ./tools/triage.sh, then git status --porcelain in the superproject. coverage/*.triage.json show as modified, so Stage 0 step 1 stops the run.

Untracked content: touch helios/.DS_Store, then git status --porcelain in the superproject. helios reports as modified, so Stage 0 step 1 stops the run naming the superproject rather than helios.

Stale branch: run /coverage-loop to any stop condition, then run it again. Stage 0 step 3 git switch -c test/coverage-loop fails because the branch already exists.
design: Sources: harness-build-instructions-review.md section 1.2, ship-harness-audit.md sections 4.6 and 5.2. Verified: coverage/*.triage.json are tracked in the superproject and no submodule.*.ignore is configured.
acceptance_criteria: A second consecutive /coverage-loop run passes Stage 0 without manual cleanup. A .DS_Store inside a submodule does not read as a dirty superproject.
close_reason: Closed

title: Make the verifier's read-only restraint checkable instead of claimed
description:
verifier.md line 8 says: You have no edit tools, so you cannot quietly fix what you find. That is false. The verifier has Bash, and sed -i, shell redirection and git commit are all Bash. coverage-runner.md lines 8-11 make the same claim. What exists today is instruction-backed restraint dressed as structural enforcement, which matters most for the verifier: a reviewer that can quietly fix what it finds and is merely told not to is back in grading-its-own-work territory.

Three changes:

1. Give the restraint teeth without per-agent tool policing. The orchestrator fingerprints the submodule around the verifier's turn -- git rev-parse HEAD plus a hash of git status --porcelain, taken immediately before dispatch and asserted identical after. That catches mutation by any route and costs two Bash calls. Add the corresponding line to verifier.md so the agent knows the check exists.

2. Replace the false sentences in verifier.md and coverage-runner.md with the true weaker ones.

3. Route the verifier through a different model. Change its frontmatter from sonnet to opus, leaving the authoring agents on sonnet. Fresh context protects against motivated error; a different model is the only cheap lever against correlated error, where author and reviewer share a blind spot.
design: The fingerprint approach was chosen over a PreToolUse hook keyed on agent identity because it is not established that the PreToolUse payload carries subagent identity -- unverified, and the fingerprint does not depend on knowing. Sources: refinements/doctrine-errors.md points 1 and 2.
acceptance_criteria: No file in .claude/agents claims an agent cannot edit when it holds Bash. A verifier that mutated the tree is detected by the orchestrator, not by its own report. The verifier runs on a different model from the authors.
close_reason: Closed

title: guard-default-branch.py allows a commit made from a detached HEAD
description:
In .claude/hooks/guard-default-branch.py, git() returns None when a git call fails. In a detached working tree git symbolic-ref --short HEAD fails, so branch is None, the comparison at line 109 against protected is False, and the commit is allowed.

CLAUDE.md forbids committing from a detached submodule HEAD, and this is the one hook meant to enforce branch policy. It is blind to exactly that state today -- independent of any future ship harness.

Fix: distinguish detached from on-a-branch. If symbolic-ref --short HEAD fails but rev-parse --verify HEAD succeeds, the repo is real and simply detached -- refuse with a message naming the repo and telling the caller to git switch to a branch first.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. git -C helios checkout --detach HEAD
2. Touch any file in helios and stage it.
3. Ask the agent to run git -C helios commit -m wip.
4. The PreToolUse guard allows it. Expected: refused, per the CLAUDE.md rule against committing from a detached submodule HEAD.
5. Restore with git -C helios switch master.
design: About six lines around line 108-116. Note the fallback path in default_branch() is fine as things stand -- verified that origin/HEAD is set in the superproject and all three submodules, so the guard is not silently no-oping for that reason. Source: refinements/ship-harness-audit.md section 4.4, corroborated by harness-build-instructions-review.md section 4.3.
acceptance_criteria: A git commit attempted from a detached submodule HEAD is refused with a message that names the repo.
close_reason: Closed

title: Give the hooks a heartbeat so fail-open is distinguishable from dead
description:
Both hooks fail open on their own bugs, which is the right per-invocation choice, but nothing in the design ever confirms they are alive. A guard that fails open on a broken config fails open forever, silently, and no artifact would show it.

Have guard-default-branch.py and check-test-syntax.py each append one line to .claude/artifacts/hook-log.jsonl on every invocation, including the ones that pass: hook name, decision (allow / refuse / skip), and reason. Then have /coverage-loop Stage 5 fold the counts into the loop-log entry as a guards field.

.claude/artifacts/ is already gitignored, so this does not touch any tree the gate inspects.
design: Roughly four lines per hook. Fail-open is defensible only when liveness is observable; without this it is a smoke detector with no low-battery chirp. Source: refinements/doctrine-errors.md point 3.
acceptance_criteria: Every hook invocation appends a line. A loop-log entry reports how many times each guard fired and with what decision.
close_reason: Closed

title: Move selection and ordering judgment from the triager agent into the triage skill
description:
Churn weighting, blocker grouping and disjoint test-file assignment live in .claude/agents/triager.md lines 27-38. That is the highest-stakes judgment in the pipeline -- it sets what gets worked on -- and by the harness's own layering rule (skills are the judgment, agents are the isolation) it is in the wrong file.

Move that section verbatim into .claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md under a Selection and ordering heading. Leave the agent with only the artifact contract, the ?-bucket mechanic, and the report format.

One reframe is needed on the way across: Disjointness is written for the loop's parallel writers, so it needs a conditional opener along the lines of when the work will be split across authors, so it reads correctly for someone invoking the skill standalone.
design: Two payoffs. Asking what should we test next outside the loop currently gets a poorer answer than the loop gets, because the ranking rules are invisible to the skill. And judgment parked in an agent is untouched by any skill-level evaluation. Source: refinements/doctrine-errors.md point 7.
acceptance_criteria: triager.md contains no ranking heuristics. The triage skill produces the same ordering standalone that the loop produces.
close_reason: Closed

title: coverage.sh hides build errors behind the gate-failure exit code
description: tools/coverage.sh returns 2 from run_one for a compile, link or config error, but the top level only does 'exit 1' when FAILED is non-empty. A caller therefore cannot tell a build error from a coverage regression without parsing stderr, which is exactly what .claude/skills/coverage/SKILL.md and the coverage-runner agent claim the exit code does ('1 is the gate failing, 2 is a configuration or build error'). Propagate the worst per-submodule status to the top-level exit instead.
acceptance_criteria: A submodule that fails to compile makes the script exit 2; a submodule that regresses below baseline makes it exit 1; a run with both exits 2.
close_reason: Merged as fiazsami/screen-savers PR #8. coverage.sh now exits with the worst per-submodule status (2 outranking 1), and a red suite returns 2 rather than the test binary's own code. Verified against all four acceptance cases: config error 2, regression 1, both 2, clean 0.

title: Trim the coverage and triage skills to judgment only
description: Both SKILL.md files carry copies of data that lives authoritatively elsewhere, and both have already gone stale: coverage/SKILL.md says helios includes Helios.cpp (its config's _scope says the opposite), and triage/SKILL.md's Current state table predates the re-scope. Delete the derived content (flag tables duplicating --help, the scope paragraph duplicating _scope, the current-state tables duplicating the ledger) and keep only what a script cannot carry: the C-bucket argument, the calibration limits, the reporting guidance. Move the scope/baseline prohibitions into the scripts' failure output, since a skill is only loaded when the model chooses to load it and the guardrail is needed precisely when nobody asked.
close_reason: Already done and merged; the issue was just never closed. Verified against the current tree on 2026-08-21: coverage/SKILL.md no longer names Helios.cpp, triage/SKILL.md has no Current state table, neither carries a flag table duplicating --help, and the baseline/exclude prohibition is printed by tools/coverage_report.py:182 rather than living only in a skill nobody may have loaded. Landed as 8d7cc01 via PR #4.

title: Enforce the branch policy mechanically
description: Nothing currently prevents a commit on a default branch: .claude/settings.json has empty hooks, settings.local.json pre-approves 'git commit -m *' and 'git push *' with no branch guard, and there is no .github/ or CODEOWNERS in any of the four repos. Add a PreToolUse hook that refuses a commit or push when HEAD is the default branch, plus GitHub branch protection.
close_reason:
Both halves done. The hook half landed earlier (.claude/hooks/guard-default-branch.py) and was extended this session to refuse commits from a detached HEAD, which it had been silently allowing. The server-side half is now real for the three submodules: branch protection on master requiring a PR and the 'tests' check.

The fourth repo is the exception and it is not fixable by configuration: fiazsami/screen-savers is private on a free plan, and both the branch-protection and rulesets endpoints return 403. That is tracked in ss-e4a as a purchase-or-visibility decision, not as enforcement work.

title: Port helios to Metal
description:
First of the three ports, and the pilot for the approach.

helios goes first for two reasons: its shared C++ core is the best characterized of the three, and its GL surface is the smallest -- 4 files call GL or GLU (Helios.cpp, HeliosView.mm, Implicit/impSurface.cpp, rsText/rsText.cpp) against hyperspace's 13.

History worth keeping: a Metal port existed on the old fork (v2.2.0, v2.2.1 and origin/modernize). That fork was deleted and re-forked, the port is not on the current remote, and there is no .git/modules/helios to recover it from. It is gone. This is a rebuild, not a recovery, and coverage/helios.json's _scope block records the same thing.

Two obligations beyond making it render:

Behaviour must not drift. The characterization tests in tests/ are the safety net -- rsMath, the marching-cubes tables, and Rgbhsl, plus whatever impCubeVolume coverage lands from ss-or3. If a test fails during the port, that is the port changing geometry or colour, which is exactly what it must not do silently.

Scope must grow as files become testable. Each GL file this port replaces with testable code should move into coverage/helios.json's sources. That is the mechanic that turns porting into coverage, and _scope already says so: 'As the port replaces those with testable code, move them into sources.'
design: Staged as feat/<topic> branches and PRs against helios master, then a superproject PR bumping the pointer -- the two-PR rule. Do not do the whole port in one branch; the characterization tests are only useful as a bisect surface if the steps are small.

title: Audit triage verdict precision on all three submodules
description: Run triage across helios, hills and hyperspace and hand-audit a sample of verdicts per submodule, with attention to the C bucket where a wrong verdict silently removes work from the queue. If the unknown rate is above roughly a third, the clang AST path stops being a contingency and becomes a requirement for the classifier.
close_reason: audited: 12/12 C and 10/10 A verdicts correct by hand-check; unknown rate 1/241 helios, 0/16 hills, 1/214 hyperspace -- far under the one-third bar, so the clang AST path stays a contingency. One false positive found and removed (c:dead-port misread a #else arm as dead)

title: Add triage front door: tools/triage.sh and the triage skill
description: tools/triage.sh drives the region export plus the classifier and prints the per-submodule verdict; .claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md is the front door, mirroring the coverage skill's discipline that the script is the logic. The skill must state that 100% is the wrong target, report the addressable ceiling, and forbid triage from editing coverage config scope.
close_reason: tools/triage.sh + .claude/skills/triage/SKILL.md landed; coverage skill cross-references it

title: Build triage classifier (rules + ledger)
description: tools/triage_classify.py turns the region export into A/B/C verdicts using a fixed-precedence deterministic rule table, writing coverage/<name>.triage.json keyed on path::signature. Anything the rules cannot decide is marked unknown and escalated to human/model judgment, which is then persisted so it is not re-litigated each run.
close_reason: classifier + ledger landed; rule table validated on all three submodules, 12/12 C and 10/10 A verdicts correct on hand-audit, dead-port rule removed as unfixable

title: Add --regions export to coverage.sh (null-driver path)
description: Triage needs llvm-cov's per-function region data, including when a submodule has no test drivers yet. Extend tools/coverage.sh with --regions FILE: synthesize a stub main when tests/ is empty, and run a full llvm-cov export instead of -summary-only. Reuses the existing config resolution, per-extension compile rules and framework linking so triage and the gate share one build path and one denominator.
close_reason: coverage.sh --regions lands with the null-driver path; verified on all three submodules (helios 241, hyperspace 214, hills 16 functions enumerated at 0%)

title: Write test drivers to arm the coverage gate
description: The coverage gate runs but reports 0% because no submodule has a tests/ directory. Add drivers under helios/tests, hyperspace/tests, hills/tests. Start with preference loading/clamping (proven crash source), then characterization tests on Implicit and rsMath before hyperspace is ported.
notes: Correction to the close reason: the follow-on issue for the deeper coverage targets is ss-or3, not ss-vg2 -- that id was written before bd assigned the real one.
close_reason:
The gate is armed. All three submodules have tests/harness.h, tests/main.cpp and a first topic file, merged to their masters, with pointers bumped in screen-savers PR #11. Coverage moved from 0% everywhere to helios 5.4%, hills 94.3%, hyperspace 5.4%, and each has a committed ratchet baseline and triage ledger.

37 cases total, every one kill-checked -- 11 mutations for helios, 8 for hills, 3 for hyperspace -- with the source restored to a clean diff each time. Writing them found three real defects in Rgbhsl (ss-4z1, ss-wrt) and two surprising behaviours in Camera pinned as characterization.

Closing rather than leaving open for the deeper targets the description named -- preference loading, Implicit, rsMath. Those are coverage work on an armed gate rather than arming it, and they are filed separately as ss-vg2.

title: Coverage gate: tools/coverage.sh + /coverage skill
description: Ratchet-based code coverage gate for each submodule. Scope is the testable C++/ObjC core (AppKit/Metal excluded and documented). Built on clang -fprofile-instr-generate + llvm-cov export, not xcodebuild/xccov, because xcodebuild -list exits 70 on this machine (IDESimulatorFoundation plugin failure) and no .xcscheme files exist in any repo. Script lives in each submodule so their CI can run it standalone; parent holds the skill.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add helios, hills, hyperspace as git submodules
description: The three screen saver projects are nested git repos sitting untracked in the parent repo. Register them as proper submodules pointing at their GitHub origins so the parent repo records pinned commits instead of ignoring them.
close_reason: Closed

title: triage_classify cannot see API coupling reached through a constructor
description:
The classifier reads each function's own source text to decide its verdict. That misses coupling a function inherits from an object it constructs.

Concrete case, found the expensive way in ss-aio: every impCubeVolume method is classified A, testable as-is, because none of them names a GL call. But impCubeVolume's constructor allocates an impSurface, whose constructor calls glGenBuffers, so none of them can run in a test binary at all. Roughly 300 regions were classified as available work that is not available.

A false A is the cheap direction to be wrong -- it wastes an attempt rather than deleting work from the queue the way a false C does -- but it is not free, and here it steered the phase-1 roadmap for a while.

Not obviously worth fixing in the rules. The skill already says they are deliberately regex rather than a parser, precise on linkage and API calls and weak on anything structural, and following construction chains is firmly on the parser side of that line. The cheaper answer may be to note the limit in the triage skill's 'What it cannot see' section, which already lists uninstantiated templates and #ifdef arms, and let human verdicts handle the cases.

Both copies now carry a human B verdict on makeSurface with rule_would_say preserved, so the disagreement is visible in the ledger diff.
design: Judgment call on scope. Detecting 'this function constructs a type whose constructor is api-coupled' needs the call graph, which is a different tool than the one that exists. Writing the limit down may be the whole fix.

title: rsQuat::slerp reads its own output in the antipodal branch
design:
Found while reading slerp to write ss-or3's tests. The covered branches -- the general acos path and the near-parallel shortcut -- are tested in helios PR #4 and hyperspace PR #3; this is the third branch, left alone.

Present in both helios and hyperspace: rsQuat.cpp differs between them only in include style.
acceptance_criteria: The antipodal branch produces a result that depends only on its inputs, and a test pins whatever that result is defined to be.
notes:
REALIGNED 2026-08-21 to the two-phase project shape. Belongs to the port rather than to phase 1.

Different from ss-4z1 and ss-wrt in one way that matters: this one is deliberately NOT pinned by a test. The antipodal branch's output depends on the destination quaternion's prior contents, so any assertion would encode one caller's leftovers rather than behaviour. There is no safety net here, which makes it the one of the three where the port has to be careful rather than merely deliberate.

Fixing it needs a decision about what the antipodal case should return, and the test comes with the fix.

title: Decide whether the shared C++ core stays duplicated
description:
Originally filed as 'port the Rgbhsl fixes to the hyperspace copy'. Realigned: the narrow task only exists because of a wider unresolved question, and phase 2 is where that question gets answered.

helios and hyperspace carry copies of the same C++ core -- Implicit, Rgbhsl, rsMath. The triage ledgers mark each entry identical or diverged. Today that duplication costs: every fix lands twice, every test file is written twice, and a diverged twin can drift without anyone noticing.

The two ports are the moment to decide. Either the core gets extracted and unified, and this stops being a recurring tax, or it stays duplicated deliberately because the savers are diverging anyway and shared code would couple them.

If it stays duplicated, this issue becomes the standing rule: any behaviour change to one copy is checked against the other, using shared_copy in the ledgers to find the twin.

Extraction is a bigger change than either port and should be split out if that is the answer.
design: Do not decide this before the helios port. That port is what reveals how much the two actually diverge once the rendering path is out of the way -- deciding now would be guessing at it.
notes: Blocked by the same decision as ss-4z1 and ss-wrt: leave characterized for now. Nothing to port until those are acted on.

title: rgb2hsl computes hue and saturation from raw channels, leaving rr/gg/bb dead
description:
rgb2hsl normalises the three channels into locals rr, gg and bb, divides them by luminosity, then desaturates them -- and never reads them again. Hue and saturation are computed from the raw r, g and b inputs instead. rr/gg/bb are dead stores.

Two visible consequences:

The rgb2hsl -> hsl2rgb round trip closes only where raw and normalised values coincide, which is fully saturated colours at full luminosity. rgb2hsl(0.5, 1.0, 0.2) round trips back to r = 0.6 rather than 0.5; luminosity and saturation are both correct in that case, so it is purely the hue that is wrong.

Mid grey reports saturation 0.5 rather than 0, because the saturation step computes s = 1.0f - b from the raw channel where 1.0f - bb was meant. The same substitution appears in all three huezone branches.

Present identically in helios and hyperspace.

## Steps to Reproduce

rgb2hsl(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, h, s, l) gives s = 0.5; an achromatic colour has no saturation.
rgb2hsl(0.5, 1.0, 0.2, ...) followed by hsl2rgb(h, s, l, ...) gives r = 0.6 for an input of 0.5.

Both pinned as CHARACTERIZATION cases in helios/tests/test_rgbhsl.cpp.
design: Same root cause for both symptoms, so one fix. Found while writing the first Rgbhsl coverage tests, helios PR #1.
acceptance_criteria: Hue and saturation derive from the normalised values; mid grey reports s = 0; the round trip closes for partially saturated colours; both characterization cases are replaced.
notes:
REALIGNED 2026-08-21 to the two-phase project shape. Same reasoning as ss-4z1: a behaviour decision belonging to the port, not standalone maintenance.

Pinned by two characterization cases, rgb2hsl_does_not_round_trip_partially_saturated_colours and rgb2hsl_saturation_uses_the_raw_channel_not_the_normalised_one, in both helios and hyperspace. Those are the safety net for the port, and the reason this can safely wait.

title: rgb2hsl reads luminosity from the wrong channel in huezones 2 and 3
description:
rgb2hsl sorts its input into one of six huezones, then a switch reads luminosity off the channel that zone says is largest. The grouping is {0,5}->r, {1,2}->g, {3,4}->b, and two of those are wrong.

Zone 2 is r<g with b>g, where blue is the largest channel, but it is grouped with 1 and gets l=g. Zone 3 is r<g with r<b<=g, where green is largest, but it is grouped with 4 and gets l=b. The correct grouping is {1,3}->g and {2,4}->b.

For any colour landing in those zones, l comes back as neither the largest channel nor anything else meaningful, and the rgb2hsl -> hsl2rgb round trip cannot close.

Present identically in helios and hyperspace (shared_copy: identical on the Rgbhsl entries).

## Steps to Reproduce

rgb2hsl(0.25, 0.5, 0.8, h, s, l) gives l = 0.5; the largest channel is 0.8.
rgb2hsl(0.25, 0.9, 0.5, h, s, l) gives l = 0.5; the largest channel is 0.9.

Both are pinned by rgb2hsl_luminosity_is_wrong_in_huezones_two_and_three in helios/tests/test_rgbhsl.cpp, which is a CHARACTERIZATION case and will fail when this is fixed. Replace it with the largest-channel expectation rather than retuning it.
design: Found while writing the first coverage tests for Rgbhsl, helios PR #1. Left unfixed there deliberately so the tests land first and the fix has something to move against.
acceptance_criteria: l equals max(r,g,b) for every input; the round trip closes for colours in zones 2 and 3; the characterization case is replaced.
notes:
REALIGNED 2026-08-21 to the two-phase project shape.

This is not phase 1 work and should not be fixed as standalone maintenance. It is a behaviour decision that belongs to the port of the submodule that contains it (ss-z2c for helios, ss-a4a for hyperspace).

The reasoning: the decision already taken was to leave it characterized rather than fix it, because fixing it changes what the savers render and the current output is arguably the spec for 20-year-old vendored code. Under phase 2 that decision gets made anyway -- the port touches this code, and at that point you either preserve the behaviour deliberately or change it deliberately. Doing it now would be a rendering change with no port to justify it; doing it never would leave an undocumented trap.

What phase 1 already contributed here is the thing that matters: rgb2hsl_luminosity_is_wrong_in_huezones_two_and_three pins the current behaviour in both submodules and says what correct would be. That test is the safety net. If the port changes this by accident, the test fails; if it changes it on purpose, the test gets replaced.

title: Narrow the gh pr permission so merging is a deliberate act
description:
.claude/settings.local.json pre-approves Bash(gh pr *), which includes gh pr merge. Meanwhile no repo in the project has any server-side review gate today -- verified in both audits: no .github/workflows anywhere, no branch protection, and the already-merged screen-savers PR #3 shows empty statusCheckRollup, reviewDecision and latestReviews. So the freehand merge path is wide open in a design that treats independent review as load-bearing.

Narrow the allow entry to the read and create verbs, or add Bash(gh pr merge:*) to permissions.deny in settings.json, which takes precedence.

State the limit honestly when doing it: this constrains only the hand-typed path. A merge performed inside a script is invisible to the permission layer, the same blindness that makes the proposed gh pr merge hook clause unable to fire. This is honest friction, not a gate.
design: Low priority precisely because of that limit -- it is worth doing, but it should not be mistaken for the review gate the superproject still lacks.
acceptance_criteria: gh pr merge prompts for approval rather than running pre-approved.
close_reason: Closed

title: Record the decision not to add a gh pr merge clause to guard-default-branch.py
description:
The harness build instructions propose adding a clause to guard-default-branch.py that blocks gh pr merge when the tree is dirty or the head branch has unpushed commits. Two independent audits reached the same conclusion: it cannot fire, and the effort belongs elsewhere.

Why it cannot fire. The PreToolUse hook matches Bash and reads tool_input.command. Any gh pr merge run by a ship script executes inside that script, so the hook sees ./tools/ship.sh helios and nothing more. It would only ever catch a hand-typed gh pr merge -- the exact thing the harness design says the orchestrator has stopped doing. It is also not a clause: parse() yields only invocations whose argv[0] basename is git, so this would be a structural rewrite of the hook. And the dirty-tree and unpushed-commit checks would inspect the wrong repository, since the hook resolves cwd from the payload while a ship script cds into the submodule internally.

Why it is unnecessary anyway. The case it targets -- merging a PR that does not contain what is on disk -- cannot arise in a script that pushes before it polls. The genuinely new risk a ship harness introduces is merging before review, and a PreToolUse hook cannot see that either.

Write the decision down where the hook lives so it is not re-proposed.
design: Sources: ship-harness-audit.md section 7 and harness-build-instructions-review.md section 6, reached independently. The recommended alternative -- asserting branch protection at preflight -- is tracked separately as the superproject review-gate decision.
acceptance_criteria: A comment or note in the hook or its docs states the clause was evaluated and rejected, with the reason.
close_reason: Closed

title: Give the closed C-set an amendment process
description:
The triage skill closes the C reason set -- c:compiler-generated, c:trivial-accessor, c:generated-table, c:vendored-unmodified -- which is right, since an open-ended not worth it becomes a place to put anything inconvenient. But lines 58-60 say a new reason is discussed, not a one-off without naming a venue. A constitution with no amendment clause fails a particular way: legitimate new categories accumulate in the ? bucket, resolved one verdict at a time, and the pressure to misfile into an existing C grows.

The evidence an amendment needs is already being collected -- human --set verdicts keep rule_would_say when they disagree with the rules. Write the clause into the skill: when three or more human verdicts share a rationale no existing rule captures, that is a proposal for a new closed-set member, filed as a pull request against the rule table in tools/triage_classify.py citing those ledger entries as evidence.

The same paragraph should name where the doctrine itself gets amended. It is currently stated across five files with no designated seat, so a principle that loses an argument with reality has nowhere to be revised.
design: Source: refinements/doctrine-errors.md point 6.
acceptance_criteria: The triage skill names a threshold, a venue and an evidence source for adding a C reason.
close_reason: Closed

title: Derive the loop's stop decision from loop-log rather than a fixed cap
description:
Two related gaps in Stage 5's decision table.

The hard cap of 3 iterations is fixed by impression, in prose, forever -- in a design whose stated reason for keeping loop-log is that is this working gets answered with data rather than impression. A loop still improving at iteration 3 stops; one that plateaued at 2 already wasted an iteration. Replace the addressable did not improve row with a marginal-gain floor read from loop-log -- stop when the iteration's addressable gain falls below a floor -- and keep 3 as the outer bound rather than the rule. The log already records addressable per iteration; the data is there and simply unused.

Escalation is only a success if escalations get consumed. The loop files a bd issue per blocked entry but models no human capacity, so it has no answer to a backlog of successful escalations nobody reads. Add to Stage 0: if open escalation issues from prior runs exceed a threshold, stop and report -- another run would add to a pile rather than to coverage.
design: Source: refinements/doctrine-errors.md point 5. The point is self-application: a system built on answer with data has not turned that principle on its own stop rule.
acceptance_criteria: The stop decision reads a number out of loop-log. Stage 0 refuses to start on an unconsumed escalation backlog.
close_reason: Closed

title: Unblock parallel test-writers within a single submodule
description: /coverage-loop serializes test-writer dispatch within one submodule because the agents share one working tree and one git index, and because tools/coverage.sh hardcodes BUILD_ROOT=.coverage-build and does 'rm -rf' on it at the start of every build. Two concurrent gate runs against the same submodule destroy each other. Unblocking it needs two changes: a COVERAGE_BUILD_ROOT (or --build-dir) override in coverage.sh, and a per-writer git worktree of the submodule so drafts do not collide. Only worth doing if wall-clock in the loop turns out to matter.
design: Cross-submodule parallelism already works and is what the loop uses today; this is about the within-submodule case.

title: Decide hyperspace impCubeVolume::polygonize triage verdict
description: The classifier cannot isolate polygonize's body because #if USE_TRIANGLE_STRIPS splits the loop across preprocessor arms, so it sits in the ? bucket awaiting a human call. The identical function in helios was judged A. Record with: tools/triage.sh hyperspace --set 'impCubeVolume::polygonize(unsigned int)' --verdict A --reason '...'
close_reason: Merged as fiazsami/screen-savers PR #9. Recorded verdict A with rule_would_say preserved. The call was the helios twin's existing human verdict applied to a byte-identical body (same md5 over the function), not a fresh judgment.
